construct: Type I fibers are slow oxidative fibers with abundant mitochondria, capillary supply and myoglobin, relatively low myosin ATPase activity, slow contraction and high fatigue resistance. Fast glycolytic type II fibers have higher myosin ATPase activity, fewer mitochondria/myoglobin, rely more on anaerobic glycolysis and fatigue more rapidly.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A postural fiber with abundant mitochondria/myoglobin/capillaries, low myosin ATPase and high fatigue resistance is a Type I slow oxidative fiber.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Type IIa fibers can also be oxidative and relatively fatigue resistant, but they have faster contraction and higher myosin ATPase with only intermediate fatigue resistance.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The combined structural, enzymatic and endurance profile uniquely identifies Type I fibers.
